title: Cross-functional Quant Adoption Preflight for Model Promotion
author: Maya Chen
content:
Purpose
This playbook describes a cross-functional preflight and acceptance checklist for promoting models that adopt aggressive quantization profiles into shadow, canary, and production lanes. It ties together eval-harness probes, prompt/benchmark checks, runtime telemetry contracts, model-onboarding gates, and regression-triage triggers so teams can make deterministic rollout decisions with measurable rollback criteria.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to any model promotion where quantization (INT8 / 4-bit / mixed precision) is introduced or a new quant profile is used for production serving.
- Intended for hybrid deployments: hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Not a replacement for safety/stability evals for model architecture changes; those must run separately.

Summary of responsibilities
- Model Owner: coordinates preflight, signs off on release criteria.
- Eval Team: schedules and executes eval-harness probes and aggregates slice-level metrics.
- Serving Runtime: provides telemetry, latency tokenization metrics, and quant-fallback hooks.
- Platform/Oncall: monitors canary telemetry and executes rollback if thresholds are breached.

Preflight checklist (ordered)
1) Static artifact checks (CI, required before any shadow run)
   - Verify model artifact signature and provenance stamp.
   - Ensure quant profile metadata exists: name, bits-per-weight, quant-scheme, calibration-data-hash.
   - Run liveness unit tests: tokenizer parity, functioncall schema compliance, embedding-dimension sanity check.

2) Eval-harness smoke battery (synthetic, fast)
   - Run 10k sample probes across 5 top slices (FAQ, code-gen, instruction-following, functioncalls, long-context).
   - Compare response-level metrics to float-baseline: exact-match for deterministic ops, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) for generative slices.
   - Allowed deltas: latency +10ms median, top1 accuracy delta <= 1.5%, embedding-similarity >= 0.98 (cosine).

3) Prompt perturbation and token-economy scan
   - Execute prompt perturbation suite (whitespace/noise, instruction paraphrase, truncated context).
   - Measure token count drift and truncation sensitivity. Flag if average token count increase > 5% (indicates tokenization regressions).

4) KV cache and continuity checks
   - Run long-context streaming probes (1k+ token exchanges) to validate KV cache hit stability.
   - Criteria: stream re-attach error rate < 0.1%, tail latency at p99 within budget.

5) Function-call fidelity and schema safety tests
   - Run 2k functioncall probes with schema fuzzing.
   - Criteria: malformed-call rate <= 0.2% and confidence aligned with baseline.

6) Mixed-precision and transient-failure stress test
   - Run mixed-load stress tests that interleave quantized and float variants. Observe dynamic fallback behavior.
   - Criteria: no cascading degradation (error-rate amplification multiplier < 1.2).

7) Shadow (tenant-separated) pre-production run
   - Deploy to shadow fleet with per-tenant tagging for 48hrs. Capture full telemetry: latency, cpu/gpu utilization, OOMs, retry rates, and response-quality deciles.
   - Compare to float baseline using per-slice acceptance thresholds (see "Metric table").

8) Canary rollout with fast-fail gates
   - Canary to 2–5% of traffic with automated monitor alerts and progressive expansion policy.
   - If any canary gate trips, immediate rollback to previous model; run canary-incidents triage.

Metric table (promotional gates)
| Metric | Acceptable delta vs float baseline | Action on breach | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| P50 latency (ms) | + <= 10% or + <= 20ms | continue / alert | Serving Runtime |
| P95 latency (ms) | + <= 15% | investigate / pause expansion | Serving Runtime |
| P99 latency (ms) | + <= 25% | rollback if sustained 10min | SRE/Platform |
| Tokenization drift (%) | <= 5% | reject artifact | Model Owner |
| Functioncall malformed rate (%) | <= 0.2 | rollback | Applied ML |
| Embedding cosine similarity | >= 0.97 | require manual review | Applied ML |
| Output coherence delta (task-specific scoring) | task-dependent; usually <= 2% | hold rollout | Eval Team |
| Error-rate (5xx/invalid tok) | <= previous * 1.1 | rollback | SRE |

Telemetry contract (runtime ⇄ eval harness)
- Required telemetry fields (all producers must emit these tags):
  - model_version, quant_profile, epoch_build_id, host_zone, tenant_id, request_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit, fallback_triggered, error_code, functioncall_schema_id, eval_probe_id (if applicable).
- Export cadence: aggregated metrics every 30s. Detailed traces retained for 48hrs for canary and 7 days for production promotions.
- Telemetry schema example (JSON line format):
  {"model_version":"v3.1-q4mix", "quant_profile":"q4mix-l1", "latency_ms": 32.4, "tokens_out": 128, "kv_cache_hit": true, "fallback_triggered": false}

Sampling / budget guidance
- Eval budget: allocate minimum 100k probe tokens across slices for shadow runs and 250k tokens for canary windows.
- Annotation budget: reserve 500 human-review items targeted at top-3 deviation slices if baseline thresholds are exceeded.
- Cost control: prefer stratified probe sampling by tenant revenue/traffic to prioritize high-risk/high-value customers.

Regression triage and playbook (on gate breach)
1) Immediate automated actions
   - Pause canary expansion and route new quant-profile traffic to float baseline.
   - Snapshot telemetry and capture the last 1,000 failing probe requests into an escrow.
2) Triage steps (within 2 hours)
   - Triage lead assembles: Model Owner, Applied ML, Serving Runtime engineer, SRE oncall, and one evaluator.
   - Hypothesis matrix (documented in incident ticket): quantization-related numerical drift, tokenization mismatch, KV cache boundary condition, mixed-precision kernel bug, or dataset/seed mismatch.
3) Quick remediations (if safe)
   - Toggle quant-fallback policy to float for the failing slice.
   - Re-run failing probes with increased precision (e.g., convert weight blocks to INT16 or use hybrid quant).
4) Rollforward conditions
   - Only after passing full smoke battery and shadow run again for 24hrs with no regression in top-3 slices.

Operational runbook snippets
- Canary pause command (CLI):
  redwoodctl rollout pause --model v3.1-q4mix --canary-id 2026-11-canary-7
- Snapshot telemetry export to escrow bucket:
  redwoodctl telemetry export --model v3.1-q4mix --window 00:10:00 --out s3://escrow/canary-2026-11-12.jsonl
- Trigger immediate rollback:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback --model v3.1-q4mix --to-version v3.0-float --reason "canary-regression"

Best practices and recommendations
- Keep quant profile names semantically meaningful (include hardware target and quant family).
- Always include a seeded reproducible eval snapshot used for final promotion sign-off. Store snapshot id in artifact metadata.
- Maintain a small dedicated probe set of business-critical examples ("canary probes") that are always run as first-class checks.
- Prefer progressive mixed-precision remediation before full rollback: try hybrid blocks, per-layer fallback, or per-slice precision overrides.

Ownership and escalation
- Promotion owner (Model Owner) must be explicitly set in CI metadata and on the promotion ticket.
- Escalation path: Model Owner -> Applied ML Lead -> Runtime Lead -> SRE Manager. All pages and tickets must include a link to the canary telemetry dashboard.

Appendix A: Example promotion metadata (YAML)
---
model_version: v3.1-q4mix
quant_profile: q4mix-l1
artifact_hash: 2a9f8d3b
promotion_owner: maya.chen@redwood.ai
shadow_policy: tenant-separated
canary_policy: progressive-2-5-15
smoke_probe_snapshot: probe-snap-2026-11-04
---

Appendix B: Quick reference (decision matrix)
- If embedding cosine < 0.95 for a revenue-critical slice -> immediate rollback and high-priority postmortem.
- If p99 latency > 2x baseline for > 10min and error-rate increased -> rollback.
- If functioncall malformed rate spike but latency stable -> hold and run targeted functioncall fuzz-suite; allow per-slice float override.
